title: Faster qLDPC: Up to 74x Speedup for Logical Gates | IonQ
key_facts: IonQ researchers Mark Webster and Nicolas Delfosse describe a way to speed up qLDPC error-correcting codes
qLDPC codes need far fewer physical qubits per logical qubit than the surface code, but operating on them is slow
Method measures several logical operators jointly, with classical codes scheduling the measurements, giving up to 3x speedup for state preparation and logical gates
A new logical version of CliNR (Clifford Noise Reduction) gives up to 74x for logical Clifford operations and up to 5x for Toffoli gates versus one-at-a-time measurement
Tested on two qLDPC codes, Q70 and Q102, in IonQ's Walking Cat architecture
Joint measurement of 10 and 20 operators used on average 2.1 and 1.7 cat states per logical measurement
Work is a recent preprint (arXiv 2607.16166); the blog is IonQ's own and carries forward-looking-statement warnings
quote_evidence: IonQ researchers have devised a way to realize the full benefits of high-rate qLDPC codes without being slowed down by their processing limitations.
IonQ achieves up to a 74x speedup for logical Clifford operations and up to 5x for critical Toffoli gates compared to traditional sequential methods.
why_it_matters_hint: Faster logical operations would let future error-corrected machines run more work per hour, if the preprint holds up.
notes: Company blog about its own preprint; no outside review mentioned.
